# Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0505a)
**ID:** Atk S0505a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Suttas
**Title (Pali):** Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, also titled *Paramatthajotikā* (or *Paramatthajotikā II*), is the commentary on the *Suttanipāta* in the Khuddakanikāya of the Pali canon [Bond 1988; Harvey 2012]. The text was edited for the Pali Text Society by Helmer Smith in two volumes [Masefield 1979]. In terms of composition and cross-referencing, the work directs readers to the *Visuddhimagga* for explanations of the thirty-two bodily parts (*dvattiṃsākāra*) and refers to the *Papañcasūdanī* regarding the phrase *evaṃ me sutaṃ*, differing from the *Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā*, which treats these topics in full [Adikaram 1946].
Doctrinally and exegetically, the commentary clarifies that certain questions (*buddhapañha*) fall strictly within the cognitive domain of Buddhas [Endo 1997]. It explains character temperaments, noting how predispositions toward lust, hatred, or delusion are recognizable from physical postures, demeanor, and ordinary activities such as sweeping [Narasabho 1971]. In discussing dispositions, it uses the compound *puññavāsanā*, illustrating that *vāsanā* could denote beneficial habits as well as negative traits [Endo 1997]. It also relates the interpretation of the two forms of nirvāṇa to the *Sundarikabhāradvājasutta* [Hwang 2005]. Narratively, the commentary preserves accounts such as the Buddha's intervention during a severe drought to prevent war between the Sakyas and Koliyas over the waters of the river Rohiṇī [Jerryson et al. 2017].
Textual reuse data computed by DharmaNexus indicates extensive shared material between the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* and other Pali commentarial works, identifying 67,414 matches across 580 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest shared passages occur with the *Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā* (over 380,000 shared characters; longest match §1016_0–1114 ↔ §802_3–921) and the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* (over 374,000 shared characters; longest match §230_17–261_2 ↔ §1230_2–1264_2), alongside substantial alignments with the *Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā*, *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā*, *Saṃyuttanikāye Sagāthāvagga-aṭṭhakathā*, *Cūḷaniddesa-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches above threshold were detected [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0501a) (§1016_0–1114 ↔ §802_3–921); Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0510a) (§230_17–261_2 ↔ §1230_2–1264_2); Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0201a) (§1002_4–1005_11 ↔ §1544_2–1548_11); Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0515a) (§2365_4–2372_5 ↔ §1371–1382_5); Saṃyuttanikāye Sagāthāvagga-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0301a) (§862_1–885 ↔ §1352_1–1379_0); Cūḷaniddesa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0516a) (§259_0–264_9 ↔ §552_0–557_9); Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0502a) (§1425_2–1426_7 ↔ §4265_2–4266_5); Majjhimanikāye Majjhimapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0202a) (§2034_0–2044_0 ↔ §1299_0–1308_0)
**Sources**

- [Adikaram 1946] E. W. Adikaram, Early History of Buddhism in Ceylon (1946) — Discusses cross-references to the Visuddhimagga and Papañcasūdanī and compares them with the Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā.
- [Bond 1988] George D. Bond, The Buddhist Revival in Sri Lanka: Religious Tradition, Reinterpretation and Response (1988) — Attests to the title Paramatthajotikā II.
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus computed text-reuse matches — Provides data on Pali-internal text reuse and alignments across the commentarial corpus.
- [Endo 1997] Toshiichi Endo, Buddha in Theravada Buddhism: A Study of the Concept of Buddha in the Pali Commentaries (1997) — Discusses commentarial teachings on buddhapañha and puññavāsanā.
- [Harvey 2012] Peter Harvey, An Introduction to Buddhism: Teachings, History and Practices, 2nd ed. (2012) — Identifies the work as Paramatthajotikā II, commentary on the Suttanipāta.
- [Hwang 2005] Soonil Hwang, Metaphor and Literalism in Buddhism: Doctrinal History of Nirvana (2005) — Mentions the commentary's two-nirvāṇa interpretation tracing back to the Sundarikabhāradvājasutta.
- [Jerryson et al. 2017] Michael K. Jerryson, Mark Juergensmeyer, and Margo Kitts, Violence and the World's Religious Traditions (2017) — Notes the narrative of the Buddha mediating the conflict between the Sakyas and Koliyas over the river Rohiṇī.
- [Masefield 1979] Peter Masefield, Divine Revelation in Pali Buddhism (1979, 1994) — Cites the Pali Text Society edition of Paramatthajotikā edited by H. Smith in two volumes.
- [Narasabho 1971] Phra Maha Singhathon Narasabho, Buddhism: Guide to a Happy Life (1971) — Cites the commentary on determining temperaments and characters from postures and daily actions.
